column1: # Queue-runner validation probe: steps 4 and 5 of h200_campaign_queue.sh's "First run" checklist.
# Columns, tab-separated: slot <TAB> key <TAB> gpu <TAB> stage <TAB> label <TAB> env <TAB> args
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. Steps 1 to 3 passed on 2026-08-17 and cover parsing, validation and path resolution only. Nothing
# had ever launched a cell, waited on one, written a status file, taken the lock, crossed a slot barrier or exercised
# the resume rule. This manifest exercises all of them on ONE card with ONE cheap cell, so the queue can be trusted
# with an unattended multi-round campaign or refused on evidence.
# WHY 30_activation_spectrum.py AND WHY THIS PIN. The cell must be short, real, and independently checkable. This is
# EXP-R2-202's own base/protein spectrum cell, argument-for-argument, run from the snapshot frozen at 34230f3c -- the
# commit that produced `r202_spectrum_base_protein`. The stage and src/transfer/spectrum.py have both moved since, so
# running it at HEAD would not be comparable; running it at its own pin means the artefact has a known answer sitting
# beside it on the workstation. That turns the probe into a third check the checklist does not ask for: whether the
# queue's invocation path produces the same result as the driver's on identical code and identical arguments.
# THE LABEL IS NEW ON PURPOSE. `r202_spectrum_base_protein` already holds a record, so a cell under that label would
# report skipped-complete on its FIRST run and prove nothing about step 4. This label has no directory on GPFS, so the
# first dispatch must launch and the second must skip -- which is exactly the pair of outcomes being tested.
# THE RUNNER'S OWN COPY comes from whichever snapshot launches it, which is a HEAD freeze carrying this file; only the
# STAGE comes from key `spec`. That separation is the reason a manifest can name a pin older than the runner itself.
# DELETE THIS FILE once steps 4 and 5 have been recorded. A manifest is executable, and one that has served its purpose
# is the same hazard as one that is stale.
